markdown_report:
The proposed experiment adds learned distance penalties inside the existing BERT4Rec attention layers. It targets stale-history influence and broad associations displacing specific recent matches, while retaining access to durable interests. Improvement remains an empirical hypothesis.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Masked training and appended-mask inference provide a leakage-safe foundation. Every supervised target must remain hidden, including any target-derived features. (2) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative margin p10 values and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These measurements motivate improving difficult rankings but do not establish validation performance. (3) Users report both stale interests and overly broad matches. Context selection could address these failures, although observed recency cannot establish current intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) TiSASRec separates positional and temporal relationships [1]. Position distance offers a first experiment without requiring an unavailable target timestamp. (2) ScaleRec motivates retaining multiple preference scales [2]. Different attention heads can learn different locality strengths without discarding older interactions. (3) AHNS cautions against uniformly extreme negative hardness [3]. Candidate mining remains a separate direction because high-scoring unseen items are not verified negatives.

**Framework.** Three intervention axes organize the evidence: context weighting changes which observations influence prediction; candidate selection changes which alternatives receive training pressure; content sharing changes how item evidence transfers. Their corresponding gaps are unknown present intent, uncertain negative labels, and unavailable ownership/compatibility information.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means more work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment for each dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Learned attention locality [1,2] | 3/7/7/6/5 | Originality: narrow BERT adaptation / established mechanism. Potential: inexpensive context selection / gains uncertain. User: targets stale and broad matches / recency misses purpose. Model: may improve weak margins / no established causal link. Difficulty: few parameters / requires attention and export changes. |
| Moderate-hardness negative curriculum [3] | 3/6/5/8/4 | Originality: controlled adaptation / close precedent. Potential: informative competitors / false negatives remain. User: trains finer competition / does not identify current needs. Model: directly targets misordering / diagnostic negatives may differ. Difficulty: unchanged inference / mining adds training cost. |
| Joint title-token encoder | 4/6/6/6/7 | Originality: lightweight shared content / established fusion concept. Potential: sparse-item transfer / text can reinforce resemblance. User: exposes item details / cannot infer ownership. Model: richer distinctions / sparse-item failures unmeasured. Difficulty: one network / vocabulary and export integration substantial. |

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, test learned locality alone. Each head subtracts a learned nonnegative multiple of log position distance from its attention logits. Small initial penalties preserve broad access; independently learned strengths allow different context scales. This explicitly targets stale-history dominance and broad associations obscuring recent specific interests, and tests the measured weak-ranking tails. It cannot resolve compatibility or duplication reliably.

Compare against the supplied corrected baseline with identical training settings and checkpoint opportunities. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Report unchanged diagnostic definitions, unavailable probes, runtime, and per-category outcomes; do not interpret training-margin gains as validation gains.

idea.description: Add a learned logarithmic position-distance penalty to each attention head of the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, keeping one jointly trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. Run this as a single architecture intervention without combining negative mining, text fusion, context deletion, or loss changes.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical interests and broad associations outranking specific recent matches. Learned locality can reduce distant-context influence while preserving all observed items and allowing some heads to remain broadly attentive. The quantitative target is the weak positive–negative margin tail in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. Neither the diagnosis nor related literature establishes that locality will improve the pinned benchmark; this is a feasible early-stage hypothesis.
idea.implementation_notes:
The supplied prompt contains no corrected baseline source. The code below is an attention integration component, not an executable replacement train.py; it deliberately does not invent the host's data loading, model constructor, sampler, checkpoint interfaces, or predictor writer.

Insert one LocalityAttention module into each existing BERT4Rec attention layer after its unchanged Q/K/V projections and before its unchanged output projection. Preserve the baseline embedding dimensions, normalization, residual connections, feed-forward layers, scoring head, losses, optimizer, regularization, endpoint sampling, masking, and positional convention. Use small initial locality strength softplus(-4), independently learned per head and layer. Normalize log distance by log(maxlen), using the checkpoint's fixed maxlen, so different runtime sequence lengths do not silently change the penalty scale. This introduces an initial attention change; do not describe initialization as exactly baseline-equivalent. Do not add causal masking: attention remains bidirectional over visible history and reserved MASK positions. PAD keys remain blocked in every layer. Padded queries must be excluded from supervision and readout.

Keep target construction leakage-free. For terminal examples, remove the target occurrence and all later interactions before truncating the visible prefix, appending the reserved MASK, and left-padding. Interior supervised items must likewise be hidden according to the corrected baseline. Earlier repeated occurrences remain legitimate history. Use the final nonpadding position for serving; with fixed-width appended-mask inputs this is features[:, -1], never nonpadding_count-1. This experiment uses interaction histories only and introduces no target timestamps or metadata.

Update the canonical model factory and embedded predictor writer together. Store the locality parameters in the same category state_dict, and save the architecture version, layer/head counts, maxlen, item mapping, PAD/MASK IDs, and positional convention. working/predict.py must reconstruct the modified attention layers and strictly load exactly one selected checkpoint for each routed category. Verify finite evaluation-score parity across the trained module, strict reload, ModelView, and exported predictor for short, full-length, truncated, mixed-length, and singleton histories. Use deterministic evaluation and existing ranking checks; numerical parity tolerance may be atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve the actual trained view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. The public diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Measure margins only at valid hidden target positions using a frozen diagnostic panel and separate RNG. Set view.dataset_name to the actual category. Retain unavailable flags where probes cannot run; absent product categories and reviews must not be fabricated. Learned locality strengths are descriptive parameters, not proof that users prefer recent items.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, and their routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and the supplied epoch setting capped at 200, including SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Execute on one GPU. All training, diagnostics, controls, and failed runs count against 43,200 GPU-seconds. A fresh baseline control is useful only if budget permits; historical inspiration scores cannot isolate this intervention's effect. Never read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

The chosen trial exports one checkpoint per category, with no checkpoint averaging, auxiliary fitted scorers, ensembles, or score fusion. Keep the host's splits, 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and macro HR@10 selection unchanged. Preserve the twenty-real-training-user full-catalog qualitative diagnostic, recording unidentified-item feedback separately from explicit mismatch. No hidden test access, external data, pretrained weights, ratings, review text, ownership labels, or simulator traits are introduced.

User Diagnosis Alignment: 7/10. Positive: explicitly targets stale-history influence and broad associations displacing recent specific matches. Negative: recent purchases may be incidental, and locality cannot establish compatibility, duplication, mood, or present purpose.
Model Diagnosis Alignment: 6/10. Positive: provides a controlled representation intervention to test against the observed weak margin tails and wrong-rank rates. Negative: history dependence has not been causally measured, and training margins may change without improving validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class LocalityAttention(nn.Module):
    """Integrate inside ONE existing BERT4Rec attention layer.

    q, k, v: baseline projected tensors, shape B x H x L x D.
    padding_mask: B x L bool, True means PAD/key blocked.
    Returned heads require the baseline's existing output projection.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_heads, maxlen, dropout_p):
        super().__init__()
        if num_heads < 1 or maxlen < 2:
            raise ValueError('Invalid attention configuration')
        if not 0.0 <= dropout_p < 1.0:
            raise ValueError('Invalid attention dropout')
        self.num_heads = int(num_heads)
        self.maxlen = int(maxlen)
        self.dropout_p = float(dropout_p)
        self.locality_raw = nn.Parameter(torch.full((num_heads,), -4.0))

    def forward(self, q, k, v, padding_mask):
        if q.ndim != 4 or q.shape != k.shape or q.shape != v.shape:
            raise ValueError('Expected matching B x H x L x D projections')
        batch, heads, length, _ = q.shape
        if heads != self.num_heads or not 1 <= length <= self.maxlen:
            raise ValueError('Attention configuration mismatch')
        if padding_mask.shape != (batch, length):
            raise ValueError('Expected B x L padding mask')
        if padding_mask.dtype != torch.bool:
            raise ValueError('padding_mask must be boolean')
        if padding_mask.device != q.device:
            raise ValueError('Padding mask and projections must share device')
        if bool(padding_mask.all(dim=1).any()):
            raise ValueError('Every row must contain a visible token or MASK')

        positions = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)
        distance = (positions[:, None] - positions[None, :]).abs().float()
        distance = torch.log1p(distance) / math.log(self.maxlen)
        strength = F.softplus(self.locality_raw.float())
        bias = -strength[None, :, None, None] * distance[None, None, :, :]
        bias = bias.expand(batch, -1, -1, -1)
        bias = bias.masked_fill(padding_mask[:, None, None, :], float('-inf'))

        # Float attention masks use additive logits; no causal mask is added.
        attended = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q, k, v,
            attn_mask=bias.to(dtype=q.dtype),
            dropout_p=self.dropout_p if self.training else 0.0,
            is_causal=False,
        )
        # PAD queries are excluded from subsequent readout and supervision.
        return attended.masked_fill(padding_mask[:, None, :, None], 0.0)


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    # Compatible with LEFT padding and internal PAD holes; PAD=0.
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions[None, :].expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1
    ).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty sequence')
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    return features[rows, last]


# Required integration into the supplied corrected baseline:
# 1. DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; retain all four routes.
# 2. Add one LocalityAttention to each original bidirectional layer.
#    Preserve existing Q/K/V and output projections and all other blocks.
# 3. Retain leakage-free sample_batch and masked-target losses unchanged.
# 4. Train seed 42, <=200 epochs, exactly 200 batches/epoch, one GPU.
# 5. Select by unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
# 6. Save ONE selected state_dict/category including locality_raw parameters.
# 7. Update the canonical predictor writer and factory with this architecture.
# 8. Strictly reload; verify trained/reloaded/ModelView/export score parity.
# 9. Preserve required diagnostic APIs and their measured definitions.
# No independent scorers, checkpoint averaging, or inference-time augmentation.

originality.positive: A narrow per-head locality intervention provides a controlled alternative to deleting older context in corrected BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: Relative-position attention and learned locality have established precedents; this is an adaptation rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A low-parameter experiment can determine whether context weighting deserves further study before adding timestamp or content features.
future_potential.negative: Recency may obscure durable preferences, and neither diagnostic margins nor related papers establish gains on the pinned benchmark.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds only one scalar per attention head and needs no additional data, fitted model, or candidate-mining computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires modifying the actual attention path, preserving padding behavior, and updating checkpoint reconstruction and the embedded predictor consistently.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models positional and time-interval relationships in sequential recommendation.
Motivates separating positional locality from timestamp-dependent extensions.
limitations: Its causal backbone and temporal mechanism differ from the proposed bidirectional masked BERT4Rec experiment.
Does not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: ScaleRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes learned locality and aggregation across preference scales.
Motivates retaining access to older interactions while learning context weighting.
limitations: The proposed logarithmic per-head penalty is an adaptation, not a reproduction of its Gaussian locality mechanism.
The supplied evidence does not validate this intervention under the required protocol.

related_work.title: AHNS: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling for Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Motivates adapting negative hardness rather than always selecting extreme competitors.
Supports candidate selection as a separate experimental direction.
limitations: Evidence concerns collaborative filtering; transfer to masked sequential recommendation remains uncertain.
Hardness does not establish whether an unseen item is irrelevant to the user.
